properties.region: Netherlands (European) -- Amsterdam Mean Time
properties.note: The Netherlands kept Amsterdam Mean Time; IANA's default Europe/Amsterdam is a link to Brussels (GMT) for this era.

properties.region: Iceland -- 1 hour behind GMT (summer time to GMT), 1908-1968
properties.note: Iceland stood 1 hour behind GMT (15W), with summer time raising the clock to GMT, from 1908 until it adopted permanent GMT in 1968; IANA's default Atlantic/Reykjavik is a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT) for this era.

properties.region: Luxembourg -- Central European Time (CET) from 1904, vs default Brussels (WET)
properties.note: Luxembourg kept Central European Time (UTC+1) from 1904, switching to Western European Time only in 1918, whereas IANA's default Europe/Luxembourg (a link to Brussels = WET) serves UTC+0 for 1904-1918; their WET-era summer-time dates also differ. Applied through the 1940 occupation switch to CET.

properties.region: Norway -- uniform CET from 1895 (summer-time years differ from default Berlin)
properties.note: Norway kept uniform Central European Time from 1895, but its summer-time years (1916, 1940-1945, 1959-1965) differ from Germany's, so IANA's default Europe/Oslo (a link to Berlin) is a full hour off in 1917-1918, 1945-1949 and 1959-1965. Pre-1895 town-by-town local mean time is deferred to a nearest-city pass (Phase 2).

properties.region: Sweden -- Swedish Time (+1:00:14) 1879-1900, then CET; summer time only 1916
properties.note: Sweden's national time was +1:00:14 (Swedish Time) 1879-1900, then CET, with summer time only in 1916 -- so IANA's default Europe/Stockholm (a link to Berlin) is 1-2 hours off in 1917-1918 and 1940-1949, when Germany kept DST and neutral Sweden did not. Pre-1879 town-by-town local mean time is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Denmark -- Copenhagen MT +0:50:20 (1890-1894), CET from 1894; summer-time years differ from Berlin
properties.note: Denmark took a national standard in 1890 (Copenhagen Mean Time, +0:50:20), then CET from 1894, with summer time in 1916 and 1940-1948 (occupation/postwar) on dates unlike Germany's -- so IANA's default Europe/Copenhagen (a link to Berlin) is off in 1917-1918, 1940 and 1945-1949 (Germany kept DST, incl. summer 1949; Denmark did not). NE separates Greenland/Faroe as their own zones. Pre-1890 town LMT is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Aruba -- -4:30 (1912-1965), then -4:00 (AST); vs default link to Puerto Rico (-4:00)
properties.note: Aruba kept -4:30 from 12 Feb 1912 until 1 Jan 1965, then -4:00 (AST) -- Shanks Time Table #3, shared with Curacao. IANA's default America/Aruba is a link to America/Puerto_Rico (-4:00 from 1899, -3:00 Atlantic War Time 1942-1945), so the default is 30 min fast across 1912-1965 and 90 min off in 1942-1945. Pre-1912 island LMT (-4:40:24) is deferred with the LMT era.

properties.region: Curacao -- -4:30 (1912-1965), then -4:00 (AST); vs default link to Puerto Rico (-4:00)
properties.note: Curacao kept -4:30 from 12 Feb 1912 until 1 Jan 1965, then -4:00 (AST) -- Shanks Time Table #3. IANA's default America/Curacao is a link to America/Puerto_Rico (-4:00 from 1899, -3:00 Atlantic War Time 1942-1945), so the default is 30 min fast across 1912-1965 and 90 min off in 1942-1945. The northern SSS islands (Sint Maarten/Saba, Shanks -4:00) and Bonaire (Shanks -4:33) are deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Equatorial Guinea -- GMT (1912-1963); vs default link to Lagos (WAT +1:00 from 1919)
properties.note: Equatorial Guinea kept GMT from 1912 until 15 Dec 1963, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Malabo is a link to Africa/Lagos, which went to WAT (+1:00) permanently in 1919, so the default is a full hour fast across 1919-1963. Pre-1912 island/town LMT (Malabo +0:35:08) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Niger (Niamey / western division) -- -1:00 (1912-1934) then GMT (1934-1960); vs default link to Lagos
properties.note: The Niamey/western division of Niger kept -1:00 from 1912, GMT from 26 Feb 1934, then WAT (+1:00) from 1960 -- Shanks Time Table #2, which IANA models for all of Niger as Africa/Niamey. IANA's default Africa/Niamey is a link to Africa/Lagos (+0:30 then WAT +1:00 from 1919), so the default is 1.5-2 h off across 1912-1934 and a full hour off across 1934-1960. Shanks's eastern (+1:00) and central (GMT-to-1960) divisions are extra granularity beyond IANA and are deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Tanzania (mainland / Dar es Salaam) -- EAT (+3:00) 1931-1948, +2:45 1948-1961; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Mainland Tanzania kept EAT (+3:00) from 1931, +2:45 from 1948, then EAT again from 1961 -- Shanks Time Table #2, which IANA models for all of Tanzania as Africa/Dar_es_Salaam. IANA's default Africa/Dar_es_Salaam is a link to Africa/Nairobi, which observed +2:30 (1936-1942) then +3:00, so the default is 30 min slow across 1937-1942 and 15 min fast across 1948-1961. Zanzibar's +2:30 (1931-1940, Shanks Time Table #1) is extra granularity beyond IANA and is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Senegal (whole country) -- -1:00 (1912-1941); vs default link to Abidjan (GMT)
properties.note: Senegal (the AOF capital colony) kept -1:00 from 1912 until 1 Jun 1941, then GMT -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Dakar is a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT), so the default is a full hour fast across 1912-1941. Pre-1912 town LMT (Dakar -1:09:44) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Guinea -- GMT (1912-1934) then -1:00 (1934-1960); vs default link to Abidjan (GMT)
properties.note: Guinea kept GMT from 1912, -1:00 from 26 Feb 1934, then GMT again from 1960 -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Conakry is a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT), so the default is a full hour fast across 1934-1960. Pre-1912 town LMT (Conakry -0:54:52) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Mauritania -- GMT (1912-1934) then -1:00 (1934-1960); vs default link to Abidjan (GMT)
properties.note: Mauritania kept GMT from 1912, -1:00 from 26 Feb 1934, then GMT again from 28 Nov 1960 -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Nouakchott is a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT), so the default is a full hour fast across 1934-1960. Pre-1912 town LMT (Nouakchott -1:03:48) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Mali (Bamako / southern division, Shanks Time Table #2) -- GMT (1912-1934) then -1:00 (1934-1960); vs default link to Abidjan (GMT)
properties.note: Southern Mali (Bamako = div 2) kept GMT from 1912, -1:00 from 26 Feb 1934, then GMT again from 20 Jun 1960 -- Shanks Time Table #2, which IANA models for all of Mali as Africa/Bamako (Timbuktu is a link to Bamako). IANA's default Africa/Bamako is itself a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT), so the default is a full hour fast across 1934-1960. Shanks's northern GMT-throughout division (Time Table #1) equals the default and needs no correction. Pre-1912 town LMT (Bamako -0:32:00) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: The Gambia -- Banjul Mean Time -1:06:36 (1912-1933) then -1:00 (1933-1942); vs default link to Abidjan (GMT)
properties.note: The Gambia kept Banjul Mean Time (-1:06:36) from 1912, GMT-1 from 1 Apr 1933, then GMT (a war-time measure, made permanent 1946) from 1 Feb 1942. IANA's default Africa/Banjul is a link to Africa/Abidjan (GMT), so the default is >1 h off across 1912-1933 and a full hour off across 1933-1942. The two transition dates are IANA's ordinance-sourced values (P Chan 2020); Shanks prints 1935 and 1964 (deferred as errors). Pre-1912 town LMT is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Benin (whole country) -- GMT (1912-1934); vs default link to Lagos (WAT +1:00 from 1919)
properties.note: Benin (Dahomey) kept GMT from 1912 until 26 Feb 1934, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Porto-Novo is a link to Africa/Lagos, which went to WAT (+1:00) permanently in 1919, so the default is a full hour fast across 1919-1934. tzdb endorses this date ("go with Shanks & Pottenger" over Whitman's 1946). Pre-1912 town LMT (Porto-Novo +0:10:28) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Cameroon (whole country) -- WAT (+1:00) from 1912; vs default link to Lagos (GMT/+0:30 until 1919)
properties.note: Cameroon kept town LMT until 1 Jan 1912, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Douala is a link to Africa/Lagos, which ran LMT (+0:13:35) then +0:30 and did not reach WAT (+1:00) until 1 Sep 1919, so the default is 30-47 min slow across 1912-1919. 960/960 vs backzone Africa/Douala. Pre-1912 town LMT (Douala +0:38:48) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Central African Republic (whole country) -- WAT (+1:00) from 1912; vs default link to Lagos
properties.note: The Central African Republic (Ubangi-Shari) kept town LMT until 1 Jan 1912, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Bangui is a link to Africa/Lagos, which reached WAT only on 1 Sep 1919, so the default is 30-47 min slow across 1912-1919. 960/960 vs backzone Africa/Bangui. Pre-1912 town LMT (Bangui +1:14:20) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Congo (Brazzaville) -- WAT (+1:00) from 1912; vs default link to Lagos
properties.note: The Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville) kept town LMT until 1 Jan 1912, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Brazzaville is a link to Africa/Lagos, which reached WAT only on 1 Sep 1919, so the default is 30-47 min slow across 1912-1919. 960/960 vs backzone Africa/Brazzaville. Pre-1912 town LMT (Brazzaville +1:01:08) is deferred (Phase 2). (Zaire/Congo-Kinshasa is a two-zone country -- +1:00 west, +2:00 east -- deferred as a separate follow-up.)

properties.region: Gabon (whole country) -- WAT (+1:00) from 1912; vs default link to Lagos
properties.note: Gabon kept town LMT until 1 Jan 1912, then WAT (+1:00) -- one national time table. IANA's default Africa/Libreville is a link to Africa/Lagos, which reached WAT only on 1 Sep 1919, so the default is 30-47 min slow across 1912-1919. 960/960 vs backzone Africa/Libreville. Pre-1912 town LMT (Libreville +0:37:48) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Angola (whole country) -- Luanda MT (+0:52) 1892-1911, then WAT (+1:00); vs default link to Lagos
properties.note: Angola standardized early: Luanda Mean Time (+0:52:04, meridian 13E01) from 1 Jan 1892, then WAT (+1:00) from 26 May 1911. IANA's default Africa/Luanda is a link to Africa/Lagos, which ran LMT/GMT/+0:30 and reached WAT only on 1 Sep 1919, so the default is ~40 min slow across 1892-1911 and 30-47 min slow across 1911-1919. 953/960 vs backzone Africa/Luanda (the 7 misses are the Jun-Dec 1911 sub-hour sliver: Shanks dates WAT to 26 May 1911, IANA backzone to 31 Dec 1911). Pre-1892 town LMT (Luanda +0:52:56) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Anguilla -- AST (-4:00) from 2 Mar 1912; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Anguilla kept LMT (-4:12:16, The Valley) until 2 Mar 1912, then AST (-4:00) with no daylight or war time. IANA's default America/Anguilla links to America/Puerto_Rico, which ran -3:00 Atlantic War Time 1942-1945, so the default is a full hour fast then. 960/960 vs backzone America/Anguilla. Pre-1912 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Antigua & Barbuda -- EST (-5:00) 1912-1951, then AST (-4:00); vs default link to Puerto Rico
properties.note: Antigua & Barbuda is the cluster outlier: LMT (-4:07:12) until 2 Mar 1912, then EASTERN Standard Time (-5:00, meridian 75W00) until 1 Jan 1951, then AST (-4:00). IANA's default America/Antigua links to America/Puerto_Rico (AST -4:00, war time -3:00 1942-45), so the default is a full hour fast across the whole 1912-1951 EST era and TWO hours off in the war years. Window ends 1951 when Antigua joined AST = default. 960/960 vs backzone America/Antigua. Pre-1912 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Dominica -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Dominica kept LMT (-4:05:36, Roseau) until 1 Jul 1911, then AST (-4:00). Default America/Dominica links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. Pre-1911 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Grenada -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Grenada kept LMT (-4:07:00, St George's) until 1 Jul 1911, then AST (-4:00). Default America/Grenada links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. Pre-1911 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Montserrat -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Montserrat kept LMT (-4:08:52, Plymouth) until 1 Jul 1911, then AST (-4:00). Default America/Montserrat links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. Pre-1911 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: St Kitts & Nevis -- AST (-4:00) from 2 Mar 1912; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: St Kitts-Nevis kept LMT (-4:10:52, Basseterre) until 2 Mar 1912, then AST (-4:00). Default America/St_Kitts links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. Pre-1912 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: St Lucia -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jan 1912; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: St Lucia held Castries Mean Time (-4:04:00) until 1 Jan 1912, then AST (-4:00). Default America/St_Lucia links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone (the pre-1912 -4:04 step is the same offset Shanks and IANA both record). LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: St Vincent -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jan 1912; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: St Vincent held Kingstown Mean Time (-4:04:56) until 1 Jan 1912, then AST (-4:00). Default America/St_Vincent links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Trinidad & Tobago -- AST (-4:00) from 2 Mar 1912; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Trinidad & Tobago kept LMT (-4:06:04, Port of Spain) until 2 Mar 1912, then AST (-4:00) for both divisions (Trinidad and Tobago). Default America/Port_of_Spain links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone. Pre-1912 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: US Virgin Islands -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: The US Virgin Islands kept LMT (-4:19:44, Charlotte Amalie/St Thomas) until 1 Jul 1911, then AST (-4:00). Default America/St_Thomas links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone America/St_Thomas. Pre-1911 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: British Virgin Islands -- AST (-4:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: The British Virgin Islands kept LMT (-4:18:28, Road Town/Tortola) until 1 Jul 1911, then AST (-4:00). Default America/Tortola links to Puerto Rico (-3:00 war time 1942-45). 960/960 vs backzone America/Tortola. Pre-1911 LMT deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Guadeloupe -- AST (-4:00) from 8 Jun 1911; vs default link to Puerto Rico (war time -3:00 1942-45)
properties.note: Guadeloupe kept LMT (-4:06:08, Pointe-à-Pitre) until 8 Jun 1911, then AST (-4:00) -- and, unlike metropolitan France, observed NO summer or war time in this era (Shanks and IANA backzone agree). IANA's default America/Guadeloupe links to America/Puerto_Rico (-3:00 Atlantic War Time 1942-45), so the default is a full hour fast then. 960/960 vs backzone America/Guadeloupe. St-Barthélemy & St-Martin (the Northern Islands, listed under Guadeloupe by Shanks) and pre-1911 LMT are deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Ethiopia (Addis Ababa) -- ADMT (+2:35:20) then EAT (+3:00) from 5 May 1936; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Ethiopia adopted Adis Dera Mean Time (+2:35:20, meridian 38E50, IANA "ADMT") and kept it until 5 May 1936, then EAT (+3:00) -- Shanks Time Table #3 (Addis Ababa = division 3), which IANA models as Africa/Addis_Ababa. IANA's default links Addis to Africa/Nairobi, which ran +2:30 (to 1928, 1930-1936), +3:00 (1928-1930), +2:45 (1936-1942), so the default is up to 30 min off across 1928-1942. 1200/1200 vs backzone Africa/Addis_Ababa. Pre-1870 town LMT (Addis +2:34:48) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Eritrea (Asmara) -- AMT (+2:35:32) then ADMT (+2:35:20) from 1890, then EAT (+3:00) from 1936; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Eritrea kept Asmara Mean Time (+2:35:32, 38E53) then ADMT (+2:35:20) from 1890, then EAT (+3:00) from 5 May 1936 -- Shanks Time Table #1 (Asmara = division 1; Eritrea was part of Ethiopia in the 1985 atlas). IANA models it as Africa/Asmara. Default links to Africa/Nairobi (up to 30 min off across 1928-1942). 1200/1200 vs backzone Africa/Asmara. Pre-1870 town LMT is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Somalia (Mogadishu) -- EAT (+3:00) from 1893, +2:30 (1931-1957), then EAT; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Somalia adopted EAT (+3:00) early -- 1 Nov 1893 -- then dropped to +2:30 from 1 Jan 1931, returning to EAT on 1 Jan 1957. One national time table, which IANA models as Africa/Mogadishu. Default links to Africa/Nairobi (up to 30 min off across 1908-1957). 1200/1200 vs backzone Africa/Mogadishu. Pre-1893 town LMT (Mogadishu +3:01:28) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Somaliland (former British Somaliland; same Somalia national table SO_1) -- EAT/+2:30 history; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Natural Earth splits the self-declared Somaliland from Somalia, but the Shanks atlas and IANA (Africa/Mogadishu) model one Somali national time, so SO_1 covers this polygon too (the Aruba+Curaçao->CW_1 precedent).

properties.region: Djibouti (whole country) -- EAT (+3:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Djibouti (French Somaliland / Afars et Issas) went straight to EAT (+3:00) on 1 Jul 1911 -- one national time table, IANA Africa/Djibouti. Default links to Africa/Nairobi, which was LMT/+2:30/+2:45 through 1942, so the default is up to 30 min slow across 1911-1942. 1200/1200 vs backzone Africa/Djibouti. Pre-1911 town LMT (Djibouti +2:52:36) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Uganda (Kampala) -- EAT (1928), +2:30 (1930), +2:45 (1948), EAT (1957); vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Uganda kept EAT (+3:00) from 1 Jul 1928, +2:30 from 1 Jan 1930, +2:45 from 1 Jan 1948, then EAT again from 1 Jan 1957 -- one national time table, IANA Africa/Kampala. Default links to Africa/Nairobi, whose schedule differs from 1936, so the default is 15-30 min off across 1936-1957. 1200/1200 vs backzone Africa/Kampala. Pre-1928 town LMT (Kampala +2:09:40) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Madagascar (whole country) -- EAT (+3:00) from 1 Jul 1911, with a 1954 summer DST (+4:00); vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Madagascar went to EAT (+3:00) on 1 Jul 1911 and observed a single summer DST (+4:00) from 27 Feb to 30 May 1954 -- IANA Indian/Antananarivo. Default links to Africa/Nairobi (no DST, and +2:30/+2:45 through 1942), so the default is up to 30 min slow before 1942 and a full hour slow during the 1954 DST. 1200/1200 vs backzone Indian/Antananarivo. Pre-1911 town LMT (Antananarivo +3:10:04) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Comoros (Moroni) -- EAT (+3:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: The Comoros archipelago went to EAT (+3:00) on 1 Jul 1911 -- IANA Indian/Comoro. Default links to Africa/Nairobi (up to 30 min slow across 1911-1942). 1200/1200 vs backzone Indian/Comoro. Pre-1911 town LMT (Moroni +2:53:04) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Mayotte (Mamoudzou) -- EAT (+3:00) from 1 Jul 1911; vs default link to Nairobi
properties.note: Mayotte (listed by Shanks in the Comoros archipelago table) went to EAT (+3:00) on 1 Jul 1911 -- IANA Indian/Mayotte. Same history as Comoros but its own modern French territory, so a separate table (YT_1, Mamoudzou LMT +3:00:56). Default links to Africa/Nairobi (up to 30 min slow across 1911-1942). 1200/1200 vs backzone Indian/Mayotte. Pre-1911 town LMT is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Réunion (Saint-Denis) -- +4:00 from 1 Jun 1911; vs default link to Dubai (+4:00 only from 1920)
properties.note: Réunion went to +4:00 on 1 Jun 1911 -- IANA Indian/Reunion. Unlike the rest of this cluster its default links to Asia/Dubai, which kept LMT (+3:41) until 1 Jan 1920, so the default is ~19 min slow across 1911-1920 (both +4:00 after). 1200/1200 vs backzone Indian/Reunion. Pre-1911 town LMT (Saint-Denis +3:41:52) is deferred (Phase 2).

properties.region: Seychelles (Victoria) -- +4:00 from 1 Jan 1907; vs default link to Dubai (+4:00 only from 1920)
properties.note: The Seychelles went to +4:00 on 1 Jan 1907 -- IANA Indian/Mahe. Default links to Asia/Dubai (LMT +3:41 until 1920), so the default is ~19 min slow across 1907-1920 (both +4:00 after). Shanks prints the transition as 1 Jun 1906 (the ordinance year); the shipped date is IANA's ordinance-sourced 1 Jan 1907 (P Chan 2020, Standard Time Ordinance Ch.237) -- the Gambia/Sweden defer-on-sourced-conflict discipline. 1200/1200 vs backzone Indian/Mahe. Pre-1907 town LMT (Victoria +3:41:48) is deferred (Phase 2).
